summary: Backend + frontend tested for Project Matrix app. 15/16 pytest cases pass. Critical bug found: /api/dashboard/stats returns 500 whenever any project exists with a YYYY-MM-DD start_date (which is exactly what the frontend HTML <input type="date"> submits). Because DashboardPage.fetchData uses Promise.all, the failing stats call rejects the whole batch, so newly-created projects/teams also don't render and a 'Erro ao carregar dados' toast is shown. Effectively the dashboard becomes unusable the moment the first project is created.

critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error when any project has a YYYY-MM-DD start_date. Root cause in server.py get_dashboard_stats(): `start_date = dt.fromisoformat(project['start_date'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))` produces a NAIVE datetime for date-only strings, while `now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` is tz-aware — subtraction raises TypeError (can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes). Fix: normalize start_date to tz-aware (e.g., `if start_date.tzinfo is None: start_date = start_date.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)`), or parse only the date portion and use `date.today()`.

minor.issue: No password strength/length validation (accepts anything, e.g. empty allowed by pydantic since it's `str`).
ObjectId(team_id) / ObjectId(project_id) is called on user input without validation. Invalid ids raise bson.errors.InvalidId => 500 instead of 400/404. Wrap in try/except and return 404.
No brute-force lockout / rate limiting on login (playbook typically requires 5-attempt lockout).
Uses `find({...}, {"_id":1,"name":1,"members":1,"created_at":1})` — works, but note `_id` projection is inconsistent with other endpoints and could break if fields change.

ui_bugs.issue: Uses Promise.all for [projects, teams, stats]. When /dashboard/stats returns 500, the whole promise rejects and projects+teams state is NOT updated. Result: after creating a project the UI still shows 'Nenhum projeto cadastrado ainda.' and a 'Erro ao carregar dados' toast. Suggested fix: use Promise.allSettled OR (after backend fix) this becomes moot. But defensive handling is recommended.

integration_issues.issue: After successful POST /api/projects, fetchData reloads and fails because stats endpoint 500s (see backend critical). UI shows failure toast; new project/team never renders.

issues: Login split-screen with cyber image renders correctly; contrast OK.
Dashboard: stat cards, sidebar and table/timeline toggle render correctly.
Uses native <input type='date'> — matches spec but note it's browser default (not a shadcn calendar). This is what causes the YYYY-MM-DD payload.

Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. TestDashboardStats creates two projects (on-track + lagging) using today's date to verify stats delta; it will fail with a JSONDecodeError on stats call until the naive/aware datetime bug in get_dashboard_stats is fixed. After the fix, re-run pytest and then re-test full UI flow (create project -> table shows -> toggle timeline -> stats update).
rca of the issue: Reproduction: 1) Login as admin. 2) POST /api/projects with start_date='YYYY-MM-DD'. 3) GET /api/dashboard/stats -> 500. RCA: In backend/server.py:407-410 inside get_dashboard_stats, `dt.fromisoformat(project['start_date'].replace('Z','+00:00'))` returns a naive datetime for pure-date strings ('2026-07-23'). Subtracting from tz-aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` raises TypeError('can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes'). Because the frontend HTML <input type='date'> submits YYYY-MM-DD (no timezone), the dashboard breaks after the very first project is created. Mitigation: coerce parsed datetime to UTC if naive, e.g. `if start_date.tzinfo is None: start_date = start_date.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)`. Additionally, harden DashboardPage.fetchData with Promise.allSettled so a single failure doesn't wipe other data.
